chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from al-Rayyan ibn al-Salt, from Yunus, who said:

The fasting person in the month of Ramadan may brush his teeth whenever he wishes. And if he rinses his mouth during the time of an obligatory prayer and water enters his throat, there is nothing upon him, and his fast is complete. And if he rinses his mouth during a time other than that of an obligatory prayer and water enters his throat, he must repeat his fast. And it is preferable for the fasting person that he does not rinse his mouth.
ai.seo_question: Does rinsing the mouth break the fast of a person in Ramadan?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the distinction between *madmadah* (rinsing the mouth) and *istinjaq* (inhaling water into the nose), establishing that accidental ingestion during prayer times does not invalidate the fast, whereas it does at other times. It reflects the Shia juristic preference for caution (*awla*) by recommending the fasting person avoid rinsing altogether to prevent any risk of breaking the fast, aligning with the principle of preserving the sanctity of Ramadan worship.
